text:
Maria (billing): :rotating_light: Pager: metering stream showing a gap → downstream token counts delayed and then batched. Customers started seeing transient overage flags around 09:12 UTC. Not sure scope yet.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423 metering-stream-gap. Pager sent to #incidents and oncall.
Sasha (oncall): taking pager. pinging eng-sre and eng. :eyes:
Tom (eng-sre): on it. first step: confirm if it's an ingest stall or aggregator backlog. Maria, can you paste a sample alert payload?
Maria (billing): snippet: `{"customer_id":"cust_42","flag":"overage","reason":"sudden-token-burst"}`. Logs show a spike at 09:12 but upstream emits at 09:05-09:08.
Raj (billing-analytics): looking at aggregated window. We see a gap between `09:05:00` and `09:11:00` for emitter shards 3-4, then a 09:12 catch-up -> counts jump ~2.3x for the window. This causes rate-limit/overage rules to trigger.
Alejandro (eng): checking streaming pipeline (kafka -> processor -> aggregator). Quick check: consumer lag for topic `tokens.emit.v2` on group `ingest-aggregator` shows offsets stuck at partition 3 and 4.
Alejandro (eng): `kafka-consumer-groups --describe --group ingest-aggregator` shows `CURRENT-LAG: 1,234,567` on partitions 3/4.
Tom (eng-sre): might be a transient GC or OOM on a processor pod. Pulling pod logs for `ingest-processor-3`.
metering-bot: Pod `ingest-processor-3` restarted at 09:10:53 UTC (kube event). Reason: OOMKilled.
Sasha (oncall): root cause candidate: processor OOM causing consumer group to rebalance and lag. That explains delay then sudden batch of emits.
Claire (support): any customers affected? I have an open ticket where customer A saw an overage notification at 09:15. They emailed billing. We need a quick note for them.
Raj (billing-analytics): rough estimate: ~72 customers had temporary overage flags; most are false positives caused by batched emits, not true increased usage. Need to reconcile before billing.
Alejandro (eng): mitigation plan: 1) scale up `ingest-processor` replicas from 3->6, 2) reassign partitions to healthy pods, 3) trigger consumer lag catch-up, 4) run backfill consistency job with idempotent dedupe by event-id. Starting step 1 now.
Tom (eng-sre): executing HPA override: `kubectl scale deploy ingest-processor --replicas=6 -n prod`
Sasha (oncall): I'll silence noisy overage alerts (for window-based rules) until we confirm reconciliation. Putting a 30m mute on rule: `billing.overage.window-surge`.
Maria (billing): please also prevent automatic billing enforcement while this is under investigation — stop any charge-run actions for affected customers.
Alejandro (eng): replicas scaled. New pods are joining. Consumer group is rebalancing. Lag dropped from 1,234,567 to 120k within 60s.
metering-bot: Consumer lag for `ingest-aggregator` now 120345 across partitions.
Tom (eng-sre): starting backfill dedupe job: `python backfill/reconcile.py --topic tokens.emit.v2 --start 2026-04-23T09:00:00Z --end 2026-04-23T09:20:00Z`
Alejandro (eng): running sanity check on dedupe: sample query `SELECT count(distinct event_id) FROM shard_emits WHERE window='2026-04-23T09:00'`
Raj (billing-analytics): running reconciliation compute: looks like ~40% of the batched spike are duplicates/events delayed but valid; about 60% are genuine new tokens. Net revenue exposure if billed = low but customer-facing overage emails will be confusing.
Claire (support): drafting templated note for affected customers: short apology, explanation that alerts were triggered by delayed emits and we are reconciling; no billing action until finish. Want to share for legal review.
Sasha (oncall): legal review loop started. Also note: can we add a fallback policy so that heavy catch-ups don't trigger enforcement? Alejandro?
Alejandro (eng): yes, we have routing policy flags. We can temporarily enable `enforce-smoothing=true` on aggregator which applies decaying weights to sudden spikes from lagging partitions to prevent false triggers. Applying now.
Alejandro (eng): `PATCH /internal/aggregator/config {"enforce_smoothing": true, "smoothing_window_secs": 300}` -> 200 OK.
Tom (eng-sre): consumer lag now ~9k, backfill still running. No more OOMs in the new pods. Memory limits on `ingest-processor` were at 1Gi — raising to 1.5Gi in the next deploy to avoid recurrence.
Maria (billing): thanks. Please confirm list of affected customers once reconcile job done. We'll prepare credits if needed.
Raj (billing-analytics): reconcile finished. Final result: 68 customers had transient overage flags; true incremental billable tokens across them total +0.4% vs expected. Proposed action: revert temporary alert mute, send support template, apply one-time credit for customers who received overage email (we'll identify recipients).
Claire (support): sending draft now: "We observed delayed usage processing which caused temporary overage notifications for some customers. No billing actions will be taken while we reconcile. We'll follow up with confirmed details and credits if applicable."
incident-bot: Update INC-2026-0423 severity reduced to P2. Incident lead: Sasha.
Sasha (oncall): handing off to Alejandro and Raj for postmortem and billing reconciliation. I’ll do the timeline and runbook notes. Tagging oncall rotation for visibility. :white_check_mark:
Alejandro (eng): follow-up action items: 1) increase `ingest-processor` memory limit in next release, 2) add consumer lag alert to paging (threshold 100k sustained > 2m), 3) add smoother by-default for aggregator to prevent false enforcement, 4) add e2e test simulating pod OOM and catch-up behavior.
Maria (billing): schedule a billing review with finance for credits, CC support.
Claire (support): I'll notify impacted customers with the approved template and track replies.
Tom (eng-sre): will open a ticket to triage memory leak possibility on `ingest-processor-3` and attach pod logs.
Raj (billing-analytics): saving final reconciliation CSV to S3: `s3://redwood-recon/INC-2026-0423/reconcile-2026-04-23.csv`
Sasha (oncall): last check ~09:43 UTC: consumer lag cleared, alerts unmuted. I'm closing pager. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
Maria (billing): filing incident cost impact summary. Good work team.
Alejandro (eng): will write short postmortem draft.
Tom (eng-sre): follow-ups assigned.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-0423 resolved at 09:43:18 UTC.
